scope.business: fully synthetic three-location general auto repair group
scope.purpose: Operational realism and explicit metric definitions for a demonstration dataset
scope.status: Research guidance; no real customer, employee, shop, invoice or account data
limitations: Vendor documentation establishes specific product behavior, not a universal industry standard.
Current documentation accessed after the dataset cutoff is used to understand concepts, not to claim that every current feature existed throughout the historical period.
The numerical survey benchmarks below are 2025-vintage sample results, not a latest 2026 national estimate or an operating target.
No tax, payroll, payment processing fee, statutory rate or legal compliance claim is made. Such rates and terms in the demo must be clearly marked synthetic.

sources.title: Request Customer Authorization
facts: Customers can approve or decline individual services on an estimate.
The shop can record authorization received through another channel, including phone, SMS or email.
An optional setting resets authorization after a service price increase while retaining authorization history.
sources.design_implication: Store estimate version and service-level authorization status, method and timestamp. Approval is a separate event from completed work and invoicing.
sources.limitation: This is Shopmonkey behavior; it does not establish jurisdictional authorization requirements.

sources.title: Convert Estimates to Invoices
facts: An estimate can be converted to an invoice that remains unpaid.
Automatic conversion after full payment is optional and can interact with checklist requirements.
sources.design_implication: Keep invoice status and payment status independent; permit fully or partly unpaid invoices and customer deposits before invoicing.
sources.limitation: The demo should define one explicit workflow policy rather than reproduce every configurable product option.

sources.title: Technician Hours Report
facts: Efficiency is billed hours divided by actual hours clocked on jobs, multiplied by 100.
Actual job-clock time is described as an efficiency tracking measure, not payroll time.
Report timing can follow job completion, repair-order completion, or posting/sending to accounts receivable; this is shop configurable.
sources.design_implication: Use separate billed, job-clock, attendance and paid hours. Persist completion and invoice timestamps so period attribution is explicit.
sources.limitation: Do not equate job-clock time with paid hours or assume all software reports use the same inclusion milestone.

sources.title: Labor Guide
facts: Labor guides provide recommended times and parts as an estimating reference.
Tekmetric notes that required labor time can vary with region and technician experience, and vehicle specification affects the applicable estimate.
sources.design_implication: Generate book/estimated hours, customer-billed hours and actual job time independently but coherently. Do not copy proprietary labor-guide tables.
sources.limitation: A synthetic labor-time catalog is an invented demo assumption, not a vehicle-specific repair quote or licensed guide.

sources.title: Line Item Detail Report
facts: The report distinguishes Estimate, Repair Order and Invoiced states, and separates invoice date from fully paid date.
Parts and tire cost/price fields are per unit; quantity is separate. Labor price is per hour and billed hours differ from clocked time.
A line subtotal reflects quantity or billed hours and line discount before tax; order-level adjustments need separate treatment.
sources.design_implication: Keep unit, quantity, unit cost, unit selling price and extended amounts explicit. Count distinct orders rather than line rows. Invoice revenue and customer collections need separate date views.
sources.limitation: The demo's normalized units and accounting policy are its own choices, not a claim to replicate the export format.

sources.title: PartsTech Seller Agreement
sources.source_type: official platform agreement, used only for operating-model definitions
facts: The agreement distinguishes a recognized wholesale credit account between supplier and buyer from cash customer transactions.
The platform connects inventory/price inquiries and electronic orders.
sources.design_implication: Treat the ordering platform separately from the supplier/vendor master and from payment method. Retain supplier account, purchase order, receipt and vendor invoice identifiers.
sources.limitation: No legal interpretation is provided. This source does not establish universal net days for repair shops; platform seller fees are not shop supplier payment terms.

sources.title: Support Programs & Services — Credit Program
sources.retrieval_note: Credit program body is present in the search-index extract; direct page extraction returned the public navigation shell.
facts: The public Credit Program description lists daily, weekly and monthly billing cycles and a dedicated line of credit.
sources.design_implication: Store billing cycle and due date rules separately. Synthetic vendor terms such as COD, Net15 or Net30 must be labeled assumptions rather than attributed to AutoZone.
sources.limitation: A monthly billing cycle does not by itself mean invoice-date-plus-30-days. No specific customer's approval, limit or contracted terms are known.

sources.title: Balances and settlement time
facts: Payment funds can be pending before becoming available; a card charge appears pending after processor fees.
Available funds can then be used for payouts; refunds and disputes also affect the payments balance.
Settlement timing depends on country and payment method, and business days differ from calendar days.
sources.design_implication: Separate customer payment date, available date and payout/bank dates. Maintain processor clearing and fee/refund components rather than treating bank deposit as gross sales.
sources.limitation: Any lag, fee percentage or reserve in the synthetic demo is a stated assumption, not a promised Stripe rate or timeline.

sources.title: Payout reconciliation report
facts: Automatic payout reconciliation matches bank payouts with batches of underlying payments and other balance transactions, including refunds, disputes and fees.
The report groups payouts by estimated arrival date, which can differ from the bank posting date.
Unsettled transactions can remain in an ending balance; instant and manual payouts need different reconciliation approaches.
sources.design_implication: Create payout headers plus a transaction-to-payout bridge; retain residual clearing at month end and distinct bank posting dates.
sources.limitation: Use automatic batch payouts for the demo unless another explicitly documented synthetic reconciliation method is implemented.

sources.title: 2025 PartsTech Report: State of General Auto Repair Shops in the U.S.
facts: The publisher reports a survey of 752 U.S. auto repair shops.
Published sample figures include 2.2 vehicles serviced per bay per day, 0.7 technicians per bay, and one service advisor per three bays.
sources.design_implication: These figures can serve as a coarse plausibility cross-check for invented shop capacity and staffing, with location-specific variation.
sources.limitation: Descriptive, self-reported 2025 survey sample from a commercial platform; no probability sampling or causal inference is established in the public summary. Do not label the figures a universal standard, a latest 2026 estimate, or a mandated target.

benchmark_context_only.use: one advisor per three bays; context only

recommended_demo_definitions.status: Explicit synthetic model conventions inferred from the sources; not claimed to be universal vendor definitions
recommended_demo_definitions.book_hours: Invented standard estimating time for the synthetic service catalog; no proprietary labor guide copied
recommended_demo_definitions.billed_hours: Hours sold to the customer on approved, invoiced labor lines
recommended_demo_definitions.actual_job_hours: Non-overlapping technician clock time assigned to repair work, including separately identified warranty/rework time
recommended_demo_definitions.attendance_hours: Actual on-site attendance clock, with unpaid breaks excluded
recommended_demo_definitions.paid_hours: Payroll-compensated time, with paid leave separately identified
recommended_demo_definitions.available_production_hours: Attendance less explicitly classified training, meetings and other planned non-production time; excludes leave
recommended_demo_definitions.efficiency_pct: 100 * billed_hours / actual_job_hours; undefined when actual_job_hours is zero
recommended_demo_definitions.paid_hour_yield: billed_hours / paid_hours; presented separately so paid leave cannot silently change the denominator
recommended_demo_definitions.labor_revenue: Sum of invoiced labor line extended selling amounts after applicable discounts, excluding synthetic sales tax
recommended_demo_definitions.effective_labor_rate: labor_revenue / billed_hours; undefined when billed_hours is zero
recommended_demo_definitions.aro: Net invoiced revenue excluding synthetic sales tax divided by distinct eligible invoiced repair orders; counter sales and zero-dollar warranty orders require an explicit inclusion policy
recommended_demo_definitions.approval_rate: Approved quoted service value / quoted service value for a declared estimate cohort and version; never substitute paid receipts for approved work
recommended_demo_definitions.inventory_unit: Explicit canonical unit per SKU, e.g. EA, QT, GAL or SET; purchasing pack size and conversion to canonical units must be stored
recommended_demo_definitions.inventory_rollforward: Opening units + receipts + inbound transfers + returns to stock - issues - outbound transfers - vendor returns - writeoffs = closing units, all in one SKU unit
recommended_demo_definitions.supplier_terms: Synthetic agreement per vendor/account with distinct invoice date, billing cycle, due date and payment date; no assumed universal Net30
recommended_demo_definitions.processor_rollforward: Opening clearing + captured customer funds - refunds - fee debits - dispute debits + explicit adjustments - payouts = ending clearing; use one consistent signed-balance convention
recommended_demo_definitions.payout: Transfer from processor balance to the bank; not a second revenue event

recommended_invariants: Approved, completed and invoiced timestamps are distinct, and declines are retained without being recognized as revenue.
Part line totals reconcile quantity times unit amount, with discounts and rounding rules explicit.
Technician billed hours aggregate once from labor lines, with allocated hours summing to the line total if more than one technician participates.
Job clocks cannot overlap for one technician; paid leave is never presented as job time.
Zero denominators produce null or N/A, not zero, infinity or an invented ratio.
Inter-location inventory transfers preserve total group units and use matched source/destination records.
Vendor receipts, invoices, credits and payments remain separately linked; billing frequency does not overwrite invoice due dates.
Payout transaction bridges reconcile to payout net amounts, and bank postings reconcile to the transferred cash.
Cash collections and invoice revenue reconcile through beginning/end receivables, credits and deposits under the declared synthetic accounting policy.
At 2026-10-31 retain legitimate unpaid receivables, unpaid vendor invoices and unsettled processor clearing rather than forcing all balances to zero.
